newsitem.title: USA: CBS CHANGES SEEN AIDING TV OPERATION.
newsitem.headline: CBS CHANGES SEEN AIDING TV OPERATION.

text.p: Leslie Moonves's elevation Thursday to the post of CBS Television president, as well as the network's top programmer puts him on a more perilous corporate highwire, with virtually complete control of the network's fate.
"It's a good move because it now puts into place somebody who can control the whole situation and has a broad-range perspective," said Hal Vogel, an analyst at Cowen & Co.
Wall Street analysts and advertising executives lauded the move, saying Moonves's track record to date has been virtually flawless, as he has steered the network into second place in the ratings.
"Moonves is just one terrific, super piece of manpower," said Paul Schulman, who runs a media buying firm. "They haven't found anything that he hasn't been able to do to date."
Industry experts said the move will sharpen the focus on advertising revenues. Being in charge of sales, Moonves will be more careful about which shows he puts on the air.
In the past, the programming chief would decide on a new show and not be as worried about whether the sales force could sell it to Madison Avenue, observers noted.
But will his expanded role get in the way of his ability to take a chance on shows that need time to find an audience?

"He will put on the best schedule he can put on," Schulman said. "He'll be even more keenly aware of what gets the maximum dollars on certain things. It will make him pretty casreful of what he puts on the schedule."
The move will also strengthen his already strong relationship with Hollywood producers, writers and actors, according to TV specialists.
Analysts said the move may be the first time in TV's relatively brief history that one executive has totally controlled both the programming and advertising sides.

Moonves, who has been president of CBS Entertainment, will be responsible for marketing, sales and consumer research, and oversee CBS Productions, CBS Enterprises and Eyemark Entertainment, including domestic syndication and international sales units.

A CBS spokesman explained how the restructuring could improve the operation. In the past, for example, marketing and promotion was controlled by the president of the television network, who counted entertainment, sports and news as among his "clients."

"The entertainment guy needs most of the marketing because he's got most of the product," said Jack Bergen, senior vice president, corporate relations. And now Moonves will be able to control how and where the money flows.
